item.title: A subquadratic upper bound for the mixing time of the Thorp shuffle
item.description: arXiv:2610.18884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $n=2^d$. We prove that the worst-start total-variation mixing time of the full labelled Thorp shuffle satisfies, for every fixed $0<\varepsilon<1$, \[ t_{\mathrm{mix}}(\varepsilon) \le C_* d^{5/3}+O_\varepsilon\!\left(d^{4/3}\log(d+2)\right), \qquad C_*=5.1536951454\ldots . \] Time is measured in ordinary Thorp shuffles. This improves the previously published full-deck upper bound $O(d^3)$ of Morris. The geometric starting point is elementary: label the $n=2^d$ positions by binary strings. One physical Thorp shuffle is a random swap layer on one coordinate matching of the $d$-dimensional cube, followed by a deterministic cyclic rotation of the coordinates. In a rotating frame that deterministic rotation disappears, so $d$ successive physical shuffles become one \emph{sweep}: one independent random swap layer in each coordinate direction. The proof then combines five ingredients. First, a collision-graph representation and negative dependence give pointwise smoothing for ordered marked cards. Second, an entropy argument is sharpened by moving an endpoint moment up to the critical exponent $\beta_c=\log_2(3/2)$, yielding an entropy-preparation clock $s^2/(2\log(3/2))+O(s\log s)$. Third, exact multiplicities in the ordered $h$-tuple permutation representation amplify marked-card bounds into Fourier operator and energy estimates on low representation levels. Fourth, entropy truncation produces a positive mixture whose regular component retains the marked-card budget. Finally, only two long blocks need this entropy regularization: a shorter third block is used solely for additional low-level smoothing. Optimizing the three block lengths gives the constant above.
item.dc:creator: Yunjiang Jiang

item.title: Delta functions, a local coarea formula and marginal distributions
item.description: arXiv:2610.18922v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define multidimensional delta functions as generalized functions by pulling back the Dirac delta function, as well as products of such. We prove various formulas including a local version of the coarea formula and we use delta functions to compute marginal probability distributions on spheres.
item.dc:creator: Ranee Brylinski, Jean-Luc Brylinski

item.title: On rigidity of infinite exchangeable sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.18992v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We ask when the law of an infinite exchangeable sequence is uniquely determined by a finite-dimensional marginal. For mixtures of a probability kernel, a weak localization condition makes three coordinates determine the directing law. Completeness alone makes four coordinates sufficient. Neither order can be lowered in general. For exponential kernels with a nonnegative sufficient statistic, a M\"untz-Sz\'asz support condition implies three coordinates suffice. In the scalar case, this result is sharp. We also characterize when completeness holds simultaneously for all scalar mixing laws by a weighted M\"untz density condition and show that statistic support alone need not decide completeness. These methods yield sharp finite-dimensional refinements of Freedman's theorem on rotatable sequences, namely that spherical symmetry of three coordinates makes an infinite exchangeable sequence rotatable while symmetry of the first two coordinates is in general insufficient. Finally, for energy-radial densities we give a complete-monotonicity criterion for infinite extendibility and determine the exact uniqueness thresholds for $\ell_q$-norm exponential laws.
item.dc:creator: Maximillian Newman

item.title: On the discrete Fisher information
item.description: arXiv:2610.19076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate a discrete analogue of the Fisher information. By using a discrete Laplacian operator, we can construct a discrete analogue of the score function and hence of the information. This provides a natural framework for establishing several information-theoretic inequalities in the discrete setting.
item.dc:creator: Keith M. Ball, Barnab\'as G\'argy\'an

item.title: Moment-optimal Gamma approximation of Bessel Process exit times
item.description: arXiv:2610.19233v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct finite Gamma convolutions approximating the first hitting time of $1$ by a Bessel process of index $\nu>-1$ started at the origin. The scale measure in the classical exponential representation of this law is obtained by squaring the positive half of a dilated modified Lommel polynomial orthogonality measure. Its Jacobi recurrence yields an $N$-factor Gamma convolution that uniquely matches the first $2N$ cumulants, the maximal number attainable in this class. From an exact Gaussian quadrature remainder we derive supergeometric convergence of the Laplace transforms on compact subsets of a common slit plane and geometric convergence of the distribution functions uniformly on the real line. The approximants have total Gamma shape $N(N+\nu+1)$, and their Laplace transforms and negative moments decrease to those of the exit law.
item.dc:creator: Steven P. Clark

item.title: Heat Kernel Estimates for Random Walks with Killing on Transient Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.19285v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give matching two-sided estimates for heat kernels obtained from Schr\"odinger operators $\Delta+W$ on weighted graphs. The graphs we consider are transient and admit two-sided sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimates for the Laplacian $\Delta$, and the potentials $W$ decay to zero at infinity. We offer two proofs for one of our main results: one using the Feynman-Kac formula, and one without using it. Our results apply to fractal-type graphs such as graphical Sierpinski carpets, among other examples.
item.dc:creator: Emily Dautenhahn, Anthony Graves-McCleary

item.title: Fluctuations in the Potts spin glass model at high temperature
item.description: arXiv:2610.19356v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the fluctuations of the free energy of the Potts spin glass with $\kappa$ colors at high temperature. The disorder is symmetric with unit variance and finite fourth moment. For configurations with a balanced, or nearly balanced, color profile, the log-partition function satisfies a central limit theorem whenever $\beta^2<\alpha_c(\kappa)$. Here $\kappa\alpha_c(\kappa)$ is the critical inverse temperature of the Curie-Weiss-Potts model. A comparison of color profiles transfers this limit to the unconstrained model for $\beta<\beta_{\max}(\kappa)$, an explicit threshold. In the same range, the magnetizations of two replicas and their overlap matrix satisfy a joint quenched central limit theorem with independent Gaussian limits. The fourth cumulant of the disorder enters the limiting mean and variance explicitly.
item.dc:creator: Partha S. Dey, Taegu Kang

item.title: Local Linearization and Exact Oscillations for the Nonlinear Stochastic Heat Equation with Spatially Rough Noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.19535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider the one-dimensional nonlinear stochastic heat equation $$ \frac{\partial u(t,x)}{\partial t} = \frac{\partial^2 u(t,x)}{\partial x^2} + \sigma(u(t,x))\dot W(t,x), \qquad t>0,\ x\in\mathbb R, $$ where $\dot W$ is a Gaussian noise that is white in time and fractional in space with Hurst parameter $H\in(1/4,1/2)$. Hu et al. ({\it Ann. Probab.} {\bf 45} (2017), 4561--4616) established existence and uniqueness of the solution under the assumptions that $\sigma$ is differentiable, both $\sigma$ and $\sigma'$ are Lipschitz continuous, and $\sigma(0)=0$. Hu and Wang ({\it Ann. Inst. Henri Poincar\'e Probab. Stat.} {\bf 58} (2022), 379--423) subsequently removed the technical condition $\sigma(0)=0$ by developing the well-posedness theory in a suitable weighted space associated with the weight $\lambda(x)= c_H (1 + |x|^2)^{H-1}$. In this weighted framework, which allows $\sigma(0)\ne0$, we establish temporal and spatial local linearizations: small increments of the nonlinear solution are approximated by the corresponding increments of the solution to the additive equation, multiplied by the local coefficient $\sigma(u(t,x))$. The main difficulty lies in handling the nonlocal fractional-difference structure induced by the rough spatial noise. We address this difficulty using weighted heat-kernel increment estimates. These approximations yield exact L\'evy-type uniform moduli of continuity in both time and space, together with Khinchin and Chung laws of the iterated logarithm.
item.dc:creator: Bin Qian, Mengxin Tong, Ran Wang, Yimin Xiao

item.title: Percolative MDLA: phase transition and critical behaviour
item.description: arXiv:2610.19622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we introduce the model of Percolative MDLA (PMDLA) on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ which engulfs the entire occupied percolation component of each particle that reaches the aggregate. We prove a phase transition of finite time explosion, as a function of the particle density $\lambda$, where the critical value equals $\lambda_c=-\log(1-p_c^{\rm site}(\mathbb{Z}^2))$. Below $\lambda_c$, the process is nonexplosive and has a linear upper bound on its radius. For $2/3<\lambda<\lambda_c$, it also has a linear lower bound on the growth rate. Above $\lambda_c$, an infinite component is swallowed in finite time a.s. At $\lambda_c$, every update is finite, but the updates accumulate in finite time, causing a blowup. Excluding criticality, the results are generalized to all higher dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Eviatar B. Procaccia, Haoyu Wang, Yuan Zhang

item.title: Exponential functionals of two random walks and stationary measures of discrete growth processes
item.description: arXiv:2610.19673v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study random walks with geometric or log-gamma increments, reweighted by certain exponential functionals. We establish precise asymptotics for all moments of exponential functionals, revealing a phase transition as the drifts of the walks vary. To describe the large time limit of reweighted random walks, we introduce a discrete $T$ transformation on random walk paths and establish Girsanov relations. As a corollary, we show that the stationary measures of geometric last passage percolation and the log-gamma polymer on a strip converge to their half-space counterparts as the strip width tends to infinity. In the log-gamma case, this provides an alternative proof of a recent result in arXiv:2607.17030.
item.dc:creator: Zikun Ouyang

item.title: Gaussian approximation for the integrated intensity of counting processes: application to Hawkes processes
item.description: arXiv:2610.19737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish quantitative central limit theorems for the integrated fluctuations of the intensity of a counting process. Building on the work of Coutin and using the Clark-Ocone formula, we first derive a general upper bound on the Wasserstein distance between a Gaussian random variable and the normalized integral of the centered intensity. We then apply this result to subcritical linear Hawkes processes. In this setting, we prove that the integrated fluctuations of the intensity converge in distribution to a centered Gaussian random variable, with a convergence rate governed by the tail behavior of the resolvent associated with the underlying Volterra equation.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Massat (IMT, LPSM)

item.title: Drift and joint minimal displacement for groups acting on hyperbolic spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.19787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We obtain a uniform lower bound for the drift of random walks on hyperbolic spaces in terms of joint minimal displacement. Our main theorem applies to weakly acylindrical actions on Gromov-hyperbolic spaces and is quantitative in all relevant constants. For discrete isometry groups of Hadamard manifolds with pinched negative curvature, the required assumptions are automatically satisfied by the Margulis lemma. This yields uniform gaps at zero in drift spectra for pinched negatively curved Hadamard manifolds, hyperbolic groups, and mapping class groups acting on curve graphs.
item.dc:creator: Koji Fujiwara, Ryokichi Tanaka

item.title: Scaling Limits of Density Fluctuation Fields of the Symmetric Partial Exclusion Processes Approaching the Zero Range Process
item.description: arXiv:2610.20050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study equilibrium fluctuations for the symmetric partial exclusion process (SPEP) on the one-dimensional integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}$, an interacting particle system in which each site is occupied by at most $\alpha$ particles. We assume that the jump rate is decomposable and that the instantaneous current admits a gradient form. Our aim is to study the scaling limit of the density fluctuation field of the SPEP starting from an invariant measure and to derive the corresponding stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE). A distinctive feature of our setting is that the maximum number of particles per site depends on the scaling parameter $n$ as $\alpha=\alpha_n \propto n^a$ for some $a>0$, so that the model interpolates between the partial exclusion process ($\alpha <\infty$) and the symmetric zero range process (SZRP, $\alpha = \infty$). Under the diffusive rescaling in which the lattice spacing is $1/n$ and time is accelerated by a factor $n^2$, we prove that the density fluctuation field converges to the solution of the stochastic heat equation. The limiting SPDE coincides with the one obtained for the SZRP. A key ingredient in the proof is the convergence, under a suitable rescaling, of the partition function of the reversible measure of the SPEP to that of the SZRP. This convergence implies that expectations of a wide class of local functions under the reversible measure of the SPEP converge to the corresponding expectations under the reversible measure of the SZRP, and provides a rigorous sense in which the SPEP approximates the SZRP as $n\to\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Kanta Nozawa

item.title: KPP type reaction--diffusion equations in narrow tubes with degenerating boundary and generalized second order operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.20081v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a reaction--diffusion equation with Kolmogorov--Petrovskii--Piskunov (KPP) nonlinearity and Neumann boundary conditions in a narrow tube $G^{\varepsilon,\delta}\subset\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^{n}$ of width of order $\varepsilon$. The tube is chosen from a family indexed by a second parameter $\delta>0$, whose boundary $\partial G^{\delta}$ is smooth for each $\delta>0$ but degenerates as $\delta\downarrow0$. In the iterated limit $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ followed by $\delta\downarrow0$ the problem becomes a Cauchy problem on the line whose spatial operator is a generalized second order differential operator $D_{v}D_{u}$ in the sense of Feller, rather than a classical second order elliptic operator. Solutions of the limiting problem need not be differentiable in $x$, so they must be understood in a generalized sense. Using the Feynman--Kac representation, we prove that the limiting problem has a unique generalized solution. When the cross sectional volume is bounded above and below, we also prove that this solution is H\"older continuous in $t$ with exponent $1/2$, locally uniformly in $x$, whenever it is Lipschitz continuous in $x$. Under the same volume bounds, this Lipschitz condition holds when the initial function and the nonlinearity are Lipschitz continuous in $x$. Finally we prove that the solutions in the narrow tubes converge to the generalized solution uniformly on compact time intervals in the same iterated limit if the tube, the initial function, and the nonlinearity are periodic in $x$.
item.dc:creator: Hyejin Kim

item.title: Entropic Inequalities and Limit Theorems in Boolean Probability
item.description: arXiv:2610.20178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Boolean entropy and Fisher information in information inequalities and the Boolean central limit theorem. We prove a fractional Stam inequality for the Boolean Fisher information associated with arbitrary fractional partitions of subset sums, and derive an entropy power inequality for sums of Boolean independent random variables and its weighted version. We then establish a Boolean analogue of Barron's entropy convergence result along the Boolean central limit theorem: Boolean entropy converges to the entropy of the Rademacher law if and only if the initial entropy is finite. Furthermore, under a finite fourth moment, in the Boolean central limit theorem, we obtain \[ \Gamma(\mu_n\mid\mathbf b)= \frac{m_4(\mu)-1-m_3(\mu)^2}{2}\frac{\log n}{n} +o\!\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right), \] with an explicit example showing sharpness. For symmetric laws with finite fourth moment and finite Boolean Fisher information, \[ \Psi(\mu_n\mid\mathbf b) =2\bigl(m_4(\mu)-1\bigr)\frac{\log n}{n} +o\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right). \] Our approach is based on the Nevanlinna representation of Cauchy transforms.
item.dc:creator: Kewei Pan

item.title: Asymptotic Error Distributions for Euler-Maruyama Schemes with Additive Semimartingale Noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.20225v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a joint stable limit theorem for integrated discretization errors of finite-dimensional c\`adl\`ag semimartingales whose predictable characteristics are absolutely continuous in time and satisfy a pathwise integrability condition. The normalized integrated error, evaluated on the discretization grid, converges stably jointly with the discretized semimartingale in the vector-valued Skorokhod $J_1$-topology. No martingale representation property is assumed. We apply this theorem to the Euler-Maruyama scheme for stochastic differential equations with additive semimartingale noise. For a $C^1$ drift with locally Lipschitz derivative and a nonexplosive solution, the grid-point error normalized by $n$ converges stably jointly with the discretized driver. The limiting error solves a linear integral equation with an explicit inhomogeneous term involving the driver, an auxiliary Brownian motion, and independent uniform marks attached to the jumps. We also obtain the same limit under two alternative drift regularity conditions based on small-jump integrability or L\'evy semigroup smoothing. For continuous drivers, the continuous-time error converges stably in the uniform topology.
item.dc:creator: Mikio Hirokane

item.title: Fitting Gaussian vectors in normed spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.20299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a family of $N$ i.i.d. Gaussian points in a $d$-dimensional normed space, what is the probability that some linear transformation maps it to the unit sphere? The case of a Euclidean space is known as the ellipsoid fitting problem and has recently attracted major attention. We initiate a study of this fitting problem in a general normed space, both asymptotically and in a fixed dimension. We specifically focus on the space $\ell_\infty^d$, where a combinatorial reformulation allows us to show that $cd^2/\log d$ points can be fitted with high probability. We illustrate that the geometry of the normed space is reflected in the fitting problem by showing that in dimension $2$, the spaces $\ell_2^2$ and $\ell_\infty^2$ are characterized by having extremal fittability properties.
item.dc:creator: Guillaume Aubrun, Emmanouil Stavrakakis

item.title: Jump limits of continuous multiscale diffusions: Homogenization under heavy-tailed activity bursts
item.description: arXiv:2610.20302v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that purely continuous microscopic diffusions can homogenize to a Markov process with genuine jumps. Consider a multiscale diffusion with time-dependent generator $\mathcal{L}_{0}+r_{t}^{\epsilon}\mathcal{L}_{1}$ driven by a regenerative random environment. When the integrated activity over a regeneration cycle has a regularly varying tail of index $\beta\in(0,1)$, the cumulative operational clock converges to a $\beta$-stable subordinator, compressing finite activity-driven diffusion into vanishingly short physical time intervals. To overcome the noncommutativity of $\mathcal{L}_0$ and $\mathcal{L}_1$, we develop an extended-time parametrization paired with Khasminskii-type time discretization, establishing finite-dimensional convergence and strong semigroup convergence on $C_{0}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$ toward a jump process with nonlocal generator $\overline{\mathcal{L}}=\mathcal{L}_{0}-\kappa(-\mathcal{L}_{1})^{\beta}$. Under uniform ellipticity of $\mathcal{L}_{1}$, the fractional power $(-\mathcal{L}_{1})^{\beta}$ is identified as a $2\beta$-stable-like nonlocal operator. We also clarify physical-time path-topology obstructions and apply the framework to Poisson resetting pulses, Ornstein--Uhlenbeck diffusions, and multiscale stochastic volatility.
item.dc:creator: Qi Zhang

item.title: Asymptotic behaviour for escaping an interval by L\'evy flights under stochastic resetting
item.description: arXiv:2610.20410v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The resetting of stochastic processes has become a key mechanism appearing in many research fields, such as searching for a target, the transmission control protocol, biology, chemistry, finance, insurance, etc., with the main interest concerning the first passage time (FPT) by the process under resetting. In this paper, we focus on the exit time $\mathcal{T}_L$ from the interval $(-L, L)$ of L\'evy flights (LF) under resetting, but we also consider spectrally negative L\'evy processes (SNLP). As the main result, we find the asymptotics of the mean first passage time (MFPT) as $L$ tends to $+ \infty$. For LF with $\alpha \in (0, 2)$, the scaling behaves as $L^\alpha$ regardless of the reset rate and the asymmetry of the initial condition, a behaviour completely different from that for the known case of Brownian Motion ($\alpha=2$). For the symmetric $\alpha$-stable case with $\alpha \in (0, 2)$, we also found that taking $r \to \infty$ with fixed $L$ yields a finite MFPT, which therefore may be used as a valid approximation. For completely asymmetric stable processes, we show that the scaling is very different from that for LF, and point out a method to obtain the exact distribution of FPT under resetting. The analytical calculations are verified by numerical simulations of the processes under resetting.
item.dc:creator: Bartosz Zbik, Zbigniew Palmowski

item.title: Intermittency for the parabolic Anderson model on spaces with sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimates
item.description: arXiv:2610.20421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the parabolic Anderson model $\partial_t u=\Delta u+\beta u\,\dot W_\alpha$ on an unbounded Ahlfors $d_h$-regular Dirichlet metric measure space whose heat kernel satisfies two-sided sub-Gaussian estimates with walk dimension $d_w$. The noise is white in time and, in space, either white ($\alpha=0$) or colored through the Riesz kernel of $(-\Delta)^{-2\alpha}$, where $0\le 2\alpha<d_h/d_w<1+2\alpha$. No recurrence is assumed. We prove existence, uniqueness and H\"older regularity of the mild Skorohod solution for bounded initial conditions. For nonzero nonnegative bounded initial conditions, the solution is positive and its moment Lyapunov exponents exist for every real $p\ge1$, independently of the spatial point and the initial condition. For $p\ge2$, these exponents have order $p\,(\beta^2(p-1))^{d_w/((1+2\alpha)d_w-d_h)}$, with upper and lower bounds matching up to constants.
item.dc:creator: Fabrice Baudoin, Hongyi Chen, Li Chen, S{\o}ren Kj{\ae}rsgaard

item.title: Supercritical sharpness for Ising double random currents
item.description: arXiv:2610.20583v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the percolation model induced by the double random current representation of the Ising model on $\mathbb Z^d$, with $d\geq 3$, satisfies local uniqueness of the macroscopic cluster with high probability for every $\beta>\beta_c$, uniformly in boundary conditions (i.e. sources). Such a result is sometimes called supercritical sharpness in percolation theory and yields a detailed description of the model via standard renormalisation techniques. As applications, we show the exponential decay of truncated correlations for the Ising model and exponential mixing for the FK-Ising measure, results previously obtained by Duminil-Copin, Goswami and Raoufi. However, our proof is considerably simpler, as it replaces the use of a highly technical multi-valued map principle with a simple sprinkling argument.
item.dc:creator: Trishen S. Gunaratnam, Christoforos Panagiotis, Romain Panis, Franco Severo

item.title: Double-arc rearrangement and the symmetric isoperimetric problem in Gauss space
item.description: arXiv:2610.15133v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We provide a new rearrangement in Gauss space transforming symmetric sets while decreasing their Gaussian perimeter. We use this rearrangement to analyze the minimizers of the Gaussian perimeter among symmetric sets.
item.dc:creator: Marco Barchiesi, Filippo Cagnetti, Vesa Julin

item.title: Two-Species Boltzmann--Kac Kinetics with Matsumoto--Yor Nonlinear Collisions: Conserved Energy and Conic Equilibria
item.description: arXiv:2610.18892v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend Mark Kac's kinetic framework from single-species Euclidean spaces to a two-species, non-linear interaction space on the open cone $(0, \infty)^2$ governed by the Matsumoto--Yor rational collision involution. We identify a non-linear conserved energy $E(x,y) = x + y + 1/x$ and an invariant conic metric measure $d\mu = \frac{dx \, dy}{x(x+y)}$. By establishing a two-species $H$-theorem, we prove that entropy production vanishes if and only if post-collision velocities are statistically independent ($I(U;V)=0$). In contrast to the transform-domain proof of Letac and Weso{\l}owski~\cite{letac2000}, which relies on joint Laplace transforms of general measures, our approach yields a direct physical derivation in state space via the transformation law for logarithmic gradients and separation of variables. This uncouples the functional-differential system to uniquely characterize the Generalized Inverse Gaussian (GIG) and Gamma distributions as the non-equilibrium thermodynamic equilibria.
item.dc:creator: Yoshiaki Itoh

item.title: Packing intermediate dimensions of measures and applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.18929v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a spectrum of dimensions of measures, the \emph{packing intermediate dimensions} $\dim_{P,\theta}\mu$, $\theta\in(0,1]$, of a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and the \emph{quasi-Hausdorff dimension} $\dim_{qH}\mu$. We show that this spectrum encodes the information on $\mu$ that governs the packing dimension of its projections and H\"{o}lder images. First, $\dim_{qH}\mu$ is the exact threshold for the packing dimension profiles of Falconer and Howroyd: for every real $0<s\leq n$, $\dim_P^s\mu=s$ if and only if $s\leq\dim_{qH}\mu$. Second, we prove a lower bound for the profiles in terms of $\dim_H\mu$, $\dim_{P,\theta}\mu$ and the Assouad dimension of $\operatorname{supp}\mu$, which improves the bound of Falconer and Mattila, the best previously known general lower bound for the packing dimension of projected measures. The improvement is strict whenever $\dim_H\mu<\dim_P\mu$ and $\dim_A(\operatorname{supp}\mu)<n$, and when $\dim_A(\operatorname{supp}\mu)=n$ it occurs exactly when $\dim_{P,\theta}\mu$ exceeds an explicit universal lower bound for some $\theta$ in an explicit range. We present examples of measures with $\dim_H\mu<\dim_P\mu<\dim_A(\operatorname{supp}\mu)=n$ for which our bound gives the exact value $\dim_P\mu_V=\min\{\dim_P\mu,m\}$ for almost every $m$-dimensional subspace $V$, whereas the bound of Falconer and Mattila is strictly smaller. As applications, for a large family of random $\alpha$-H\"{o}lder maps $f_\omega:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m$, we prove that, for compactly supported $\mu$, $\dim_P\mu_{f_\omega}=m$ almost surely if and only if $\alpha m\leq\dim_{qH}\mu$, and that the packing analogue of Kahane's formula holds for fractional Brownian motions if and only if $\dim_{qH}\mu=\dim_P\mu$. Analogous results are obtained for analytic sets.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Angelini

item.title: Wong--Zakai Convergence and FNO Learning for Stochastic Volterra Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.18939v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper studies Wong--Zakai convergence and Fourier neural operator learning for stochastic Volterra integral equations (SVIEs) describing random systems with memory. A Wong--Zakai theorem establishes convergence of pathwise solutions driven by piecewise linear approximations of Brownian motion to the corresponding SVIE solution. This convergence provides a foundation for using mirror-padded Fourier neural operators to learn the solution operator mapping initial conditions and driving noise to entire solution trajectories. Numerical experiments demonstrate competitive prediction accuracy and generalization to temporal grids finer than those used for training, while assessing the influence of padding and computational cost. As a follow-up to \citet{LKP:26}, this study extends their operator-learning framework to SVIEs through separate convergence and approximation analyses tailored to convolutional memory.
item.dc:creator: Wonjae Lee, Jiuk Jang, Hyungbin Park

item.title: $L^p_\mu$-Normed Spaces of Bounded Multilinear Operator
item.description: arXiv:2610.19151v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the spaces of bounded multilinear operators $\mathcal L^i(X,Y)$ endowed with $L^p_\mu$-norms, where $X,Y$ are normed spaces and $\mu$ is a measure with $p$-moments. These are norms without taking a quotient, under suitable support conditions. The topology induced coincides with the strong operator and compact-open topologies on operator-norm-bounded subsets. Furthermore, we identify the completion of these spaces with spaces of Hilbert--Schmidt operators on the reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) for $p=2$; with iterated $\gamma$-radonifying multilinear operators on the RKHS in the Gaussian case, for general $p$.
item.dc:creator: Filippo de Feo

item.title: With Leverage, the Gambler is Not the One Who Gets Ruined
item.description: arXiv:2610.19239v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this note we explore the following simple question: How does the classic \emph{gambler's ruin} phenomenon change if we allow the gambler \emph{financial leverage}? We show that, with a moderate amount of leverage, it is possible for an (idealized) gambler to sustain seemingly improbable profits over a remarkably long time horizon without ever going bankrupt, \emph{even} if the gambler makes only fair bets. With a leverage ratio of $L = 10$ (less than what Lehman Brothers Holdings had from 1995--2008), the probability of multiplying one's money by $1000\times$ without going bankrupt is roughly $50\%$. More generally, given $L$-fold leverage, and given the goal of multiplying one's money by a factor of $r > 1$, the optimal gambling strategy has probability roughly $r^{-1/L}$ of success. The results in this note are designed as part of the course development for the CMU randomized algorithms course.
item.dc:creator: William Kuszmaul

item.title: Weight-adapted ANOVA kernels for high-dimensional periodic approximation
item.description: arXiv:2610.19409v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we construct normalized periodic kernels from univariate functions satisfying suitable moment conditions and derive sufficient conditions for high-order convolution approximation. Two computable quasi-interpolation schemes are obtained by discretizing the convolution integral using either a full tensor grid or random samples. In each case, the analysis separates the continuous convolution error from the error introduced by discretization. The contribution of kernel energy to the error exposes the dimensional dependence of tensor-product kernels and motivates our weight-adapted ANOVA constructions. Under suitable summability conditions on the weights, we establish convolution error and kernel energy estimates that yield dimension-uniform error bounds for the resulting quasi-interpolants. Numerical experiments corroborate the theoretical convergence rates and illustrate the effect of coordinate weighting on dimensional dependence.
item.dc:creator: Zhengjie Sun

item.title: From Global to Tail Convergence: Dynamics of $\alpha$-Stable Score-Based Generative Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.19773v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Score-based generative models driven by $\alpha$-stable L{\'e}vy processes have been proposed as an alternative to Brownian diffusion models, with empirical evidence suggesting improved sampling and better modeling of heavy-tailed data. Yet theoretical guarantees for these models remain limited. We develop a non-asymptotic convergence analysis for scale-preserving $\alpha$-stable generative dynamics, covering both compactly supported and power-law targets. In p-Wasserstein distance, we quantify the effects of early stopping, initialization, score approximation, and time discretization, and show exponential decay of the initialization error. A comparison with Brownian dynamics reveals that global Wasserstein convergence alone does not fundamentally distinguish the two models: both initialization errors decay exponentially with the forward horizon on the common class of heavy-tailed targets. A sharp separation emerges instead in the tails. At any positive generation time, stable dynamics produces power-law tails with index $\alpha$, whereas Brownian dynamics remains light-tailed. For a target with tail index $\nu$, asymptotically correct extreme-quantile scaling is possible precisely when $\alpha$=$\nu$. These results identify tail-index matching as a principled mechanism behind the ability of stable generative models to capture extreme events.
item.dc:creator: Ianis Hammani (ENS Paris Saclay, LMO), Claire Boyer (LMO, IUF)

item.title: Interior smoothness and zero-variance geometry for finite-maturity Heston American puts
item.description: arXiv:2610.20000v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study finite-maturity American puts in the Heston model without the Feller condition. At positive variance, the exercise boundary is smooth and strictly decreasing in remaining maturity and variance. At zero variance, the endpoint is locally Lipschitz in remaining maturity, the boundary moves with bounded speed in maturity uniformly down to zero variance, and it extends continuously to the axis. Each boundary slice at positive maturity has a regular $C^1$ closure tangent to the zero-variance axis, its stock threshold has variance derivative tending to minus infinity, and both partial derivatives of the inverse boundary graph vanish along the slice. The continuation premium at the axis contact stock is of order variance, and as a consequence smooth fit fails in the variance direction at the axis. At expiry the whole boundary, including its axis edge, converges to the strike. We give quantitative boundary gap bounds, an exact limiting weighted boundary Hessian, and vertical identities retaining the maturity term. Exact boundary gap equivalents remain open.
item.dc:creator: Junkee Jeon, Takwon Kim, Jehan Oh

item.title: Drift parameter estimation for interacting particle systems with singular repulsion
item.description: arXiv:2610.20090v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the estimation of the interaction parameter in singular interacting particle systems from continuous and discrete observations over a fixed time horizon. The singularity of the interaction drift prevents the direct application of standard likelihood and contrast-based methods, which rely on regularity assumptions that fail in this setting. Our approach exploits an exact reduction of the particle dynamics to a one-dimensional stochastic differential equation for a quadratic empirical moment. By the symmetry of the interaction kernel, the singular terms cancel, yielding an explicit estimator in which the unknown parameter enters linearly. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality as the number of particles, \(N\), tends to infinity. Letting \(\varepsilon_N\) denote the microscopic noise scaling of the system, we obtain asymptotic normality at the rate \(\sqrt{N/\varepsilon_N}\) for strictly positive interaction kernels, under an additional condition on the limiting empirical information. We further extend these results to degenerate interaction kernels, achieving consistency and asymptotic normality at rate \(N\) under suitable structural assumptions and the canonical scaling \(\varepsilon_N=N^{-1}\). In both regimes, we provide conditions on the observation mesh ensuring that the statistical limits remain valid under discrete sampling, in high frequency. Finally, we illustrate the applicability of our methodology through Dyson Brownian motion, the Dyson Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process, and Wishart--Laguerre particle systems, alongside a numerical investigation of the estimators' finite-sample performance.
item.dc:creator: Chiara Amorino, Jacek Malecki, Radomyra Shevchenko

item.title: Gaussian rigidity and width of measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.20385v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given $0\le m<n$ and a positive Radon measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^n$ with at most polynomial growth, assume that it has finite $m$-dimensional \emph{Gaussian discrepancy}, defined as $$\mathcal D(\mu):=\limsup_{R\to\infty}\Bigl[R^2\sup_{x\in\mathrm{spt}\mu}|G_R^\mu(x)-1|\Bigr],$$ where $G_R^\mu(x):=(4\pi R^2)^{-m/2}\int_{\mathbb R^n} e^{-|z-x|^2/(4R^2)}\,d\mu(z)$. Provided that $\mu$ admits a flat blow-down $\mathcal H^m\llcorner V$ (an assumption that cannot be dropped entirely), we prove that there exists a finite (smallest) $0\le\delta<\infty$, called the \emph{width} of $\mu$, such that $$\mathrm{spt}\mu\subseteq \bar B_\delta(V+x_0),\quad \delta^2\le C(m,n)\mathcal{D}(\mu),$$ where $\bar B_\delta(V+x_0)$ denotes the closed $\delta$-neighborhood of a suitable translate of $V$. Note that the exponent is optimal because of scale invariance. In particular, when $\mathcal D(\mu)=0$, the support of $\mu$ is included in an $m$-dimensional affine plane. We use this fact to give a simpler proof of Preiss's rectifiability theorem: while still based on Gaussian averages of $\mu$, this new proof avoids showing uniqueness (and hence conicality) of blow-downs of $m$-uniform measures, as well as studying Gaussian-weighted moments beyond second order. The strategy of proof consists of an anisotropic blow-down of $\mu$, followed by an analysis of the resulting Young measure, using a rigidity lemma involving the heat semigroup.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Pigati

item.title: Loglinear Hawkes processes: existence, nonexplosion, stability and moment bounds
item.description: arXiv:2507.11265v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper discusses a special class of nonlinear Hawkes processes, where the rate function is the exponential function. We call these processes loglinear Hawkes processes. Such processes are used with success in computational neuroscience and we provide a mathematical background for them. After obtaining existence from a standard Poisson embedding, we give sufficient conditions for explosion and nonexplosion that cover a large class of memory functions. In order to give sufficient stability conditions, we construct an autoregressive integer-valued time series that gives pathwise upper bounds for the bin counts of a loglinear Hawkes process. From here, a Markov chain argument shows that the regeneration time for a loglinear Hawkes process has finite expectation if the memory function is negative enough in a neighborhood of zero. Stability in total variation follows. Finally, we show that both the loglinear Hawkes process under a large class of initial conditions and its stationary version have finite exponential moments.
item.dc:creator: Tomasz R. Bielecki, Jacek Jakubowski, Matthias Kirchner, Mariusz Niew\k{e}g{\l}owski

item.title: The odometer in subcritical activated random walk
item.description: arXiv:2510.05514v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the activated random walk particle system, a model of self-organized criticality, on $\mathbb{Z}$ with i.i.d.-Bernoulli initial configuration. We show that at subcritical density, the system's odometer function, which counts the number of actions taken at each site, has a stretched exponential tail. It follows that the expected odometer at each site is finite.
item.dc:creator: Tobias Johnson, Jacob Richey

item.title: Eddy viscosity by L\'evy transport noises
item.description: arXiv:2510.13463v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider stochastic linear transport equations in dimension $d\geq 2$ and stochastic 2D Euler equations with $L^2$-initial condition, both driven by L\'evy transport noise in the Marcus sense. Under a suitable scaling limit of the noises, we prove that the solutions to the stochastic linear transport equations converge to the solution of the deterministic heat equation, while weak solutions to the stochastic 2D Euler equations converge weakly to the unique solution of the deterministic 2D Navier--Stokes equation. These results show that small-scale jump noises generate eddy viscosity, extending the recent studies on It\^o--Stratonovich diffusion limits to the discontinuous setting.
item.dc:creator: Dejun Luo, Feifan Teng

item.title: Anomalous scaling law for the two-dimensional Gaussian free field
item.description: arXiv:2512.10933v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider level-set percolation for the Gaussian free field $\varphi$ on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ regularised by a mass of order $N^{-2}$, and investigate the probability $\theta_N(a)$ that the cluster of the origin in $\{\varphi \geq \sqrt{g_N} a\}$ reaches distance $N$ while remaining finite, where $g_N$ is the variance of $\varphi_0$. We prove a scaling law for $\theta_N(a)$ which is quantitative simultaneously in $a$ and $N$. It asserts that $\theta_N(a)=\theta_{\xi}(a_*)(N/\xi)^{-\vartheta+o(1)}$ as $N/\xi\to\infty$, where the correlation length $\xi$ diverges exponentially as $a$ approaches the critical level $a_*$, the critical one-arm probability $\theta_{\xi}(a_*)$ decays fractional-logarithmically, and the exponent $\vartheta$ is explicit and given by a variational problem involving the logarithmic energy. Thus $\theta_N(a)$ crosses over from fractional logarithmic decay at and near criticality ($N\lesssim\xi$) to polynomial decay away from it ($N\gg\xi$), in stark contrast with dimension three and higher, where similar observables exhibit polynomial decay at and near criticality and rapid decay away from it. The proof relies on a coarse-graining scheme capturing a polynomial rate with sharp exponent, and on sharp logarithmic capacity estimates for planar "porous" sets.
item.dc:creator: Pierre-Fran\c{c}ois Rodriguez, Wen Zhang

item.title: Simple repair policies and decompositions for semi-coherent systems with simultaneous failures
item.description: arXiv:2601.08786v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider semi-coherent binary systems that are subject to simultaneous failures of its components. These are systems whose components can be either working or failed; the system can also be working or failed depending on the state of the components; and repairing a component cannot cause the system to fail. We consider that one or more components can fail simultaneously, allowing us to model external shocks and disasters. For this, we use the L\'evy-frailty Marshall-Olkin (LFMO) multivariate distribution to model the failure times of the components. We aim to answer in which states of the system we should repair the components. This is a challenging question, as the number of repair policies grows super-exponentially in the number of components. To tackle this, we propose a simple family of repair policies, which we call $r$-out-of-$n$:R repair policies, where one repairs all failed components when the system fails or when there are $r$ or more failed components. Our main contribution is that we derive exact and simple expressions for key performance-evaluation quantities of the system operating under our proposed repair policies. That is, we give explicit expressions for the mean time-to-failure of the system, mean time-to-repair, probability of system-failure before repair, and component- and system-repair rate. We also give expressions for the expected cost and long-term average cost, when there are components' and system repair cost. The only relevant parameters involved in the derived expressions are the structural signature of the system, and the Laplace exponent associated to the LFMO distribution.
item.dc:creator: Guido Lagos, Jorge Navarro, Hector Olivero

item.title: Triggered urn models for frequently asked questions (FAQ)
item.description: arXiv:2601.10337v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate a nonclassic urn model with triggers that increase the number of colors. The scheme has emerged as a model for web services that set up frequently asked questions (FAQ). We present a thorough asymptotic analysis of the FAQ urn scheme in generality that covers a large number of special cases, such as Simon's urn. For instance, we consider time dependent triggering probabilities. We identify regularity conditions on these probabilities that classify the schemes into those where the number of colors in the urn remains almost surely finite or increases to infinity and conditions that tell us whether all the existing colors are observed infinitely often or not. We determine the rank curve, too. In view of the broad generality of the trigger probabilities, a spectrum of limit distributions appears, from central limit theorems to Poisson approximation, to power-laws, revealing connections to Heaps exponent and Zipf's law. A combinatorial approach to the Simon urn is presented to indicate the possibility of such exact analysis, which is important for short-term predictions. Extensive simulations on real datasets (from Amazon sales) as well as computer-generated data clearly indicate that the asymptotic and exact theory developed agrees with practice.
item.dc:creator: Irene Crimaldi, Andrea Ghiglietti, Leen Hatem, Hosam Mahmoud

item.title: LU-type factorizations and Darboux transformations for continuous-time birth--death processes
item.description: arXiv:2601.14074v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study LU-type factorizations of the infinitesimal generator of a possibly nonconservative birth--death process on $\mathbb{N}_0$, and characterize those for which the corresponding Darboux transformations, obtained by reversing the order of the factors, are again infinitesimal generators of birth--death processes. Two types of factorizations are considered: lower--upper (LU) and upper--lower (UL). In the LU case, the factorization is uniquely determined once the absorption rate of the Darboux-transformed process is fixed, whereas the UL factorization involves an additional free parameter. For both cases we obtain closed-form expressions for the coefficients of the factors in terms of the birth--death rates, determine the exact ranges of the parameters for which the Darboux transforms are birth--death generators, and give probabilistic interpretations of the coefficients in terms of hitting probabilities, expected passage times and occupation times. We also describe the associated spectral transformations (Christoffel and Geronimus transforms) and orthogonal polynomials, and study when the Darboux-transformed process again has a uniquely determined spectral measure: this is always the case for the UL factorization, while for the LU factorization it is characterized by the divergence of a single explicit series. The general results are illustrated with the $M/M/1$ queue, for which all the quantities involved can be computed explicitly.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Arcia-Manoleskos, Manuel Dom\'inguez de la Iglesia

item.title: Fractional Navier-Stokes Equations with Caputo Derivative Driven by Hermite Noise
item.description: arXiv:2604.10602v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study time-fractional stochastic Navier-Stokes equations on a bounded domain of $\R^2$, driven by a cylindrical Hermite noise of order $k\ge1$ and Hurst parameter $H\in(1/2,1)$, built mode-by-mode on the eigenbasis of the Stokes operator. This class of noises generalizes fractional Brownian motion ($k=1$) and the Rosenblatt process ($k=2$) to arbitrary non-Gaussian order. Combining Wiener-chaos hypercontractivity with Hilbert-Schmidt estimates for the Mittag-Leffler operator, we establish the regularity of the associated stochastic convolution. A Da Prato-Debussche decomposition, carried out in a scale of Lebesgue spaces $L^q_\sigma(D)$ on which the bilinear term is controlled by a Calder\'on-Zygmund estimate, then yields existence and uniqueness of a maximal mild solution, and H\"older regularity of the time-frozen solution under the condition $\al+2H>2$ together with standard regularity assumptions on the initial datum. We further obtain moment bounds for the stochastic convolution and for the quadratic self-interaction of the noise, whose growth in the moment order is governed by $k$, and a functional non-central limit theorem giving a radially localised approximation of the solution by systems driven by functionals of Gaussian sequences with long-range dependence.
item.dc:creator: Lara Daw, Atef Lechiheb

item.title: Variation and Hausdorff dimension of fractional Wiener-Weierstrass bridges
item.description: arXiv:2606.11994v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fractional Wiener--Weierstrass bridges are a class of Gaussian processes obtained by replacing trigonometric functions in the construction of classical Weierstrass functions by fractional Brownian bridges. A number of their sample path properties were derived in Schied--Zhang (2024,2026). The analysis in these papers left several open questions, most of which are addressed here. Specifically, we prove that, in the regime in which the Weierstrass mechanism dominates the underlying fractional Brownian bridge, the limiting $b$-adic variation coefficient has an absolutely continuous distribution and is therefore genuinely random. At the critical point between the two roughness regimes, we establish the power-variation formula and the critical $\Phi$-variation limit conjectured in Schied--Zhang (2024). Finally, we derive the Hausdorff dimension for the graphs of the sample paths by proving a conjecture from Schied--Zhang (2026) for the missing high-Hurst case.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Schied, Zhenyuan Zhang

item.title: From smooth to discontinuous kernels: a variance transfer principle for hyperuniform processes
item.description: arXiv:2606.22940v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a transfer principle for the fluctuations of linear statistics of finite particle systems around Lebesgue measure: if for a smooth kernel the variance decays polynomially with some exponent a compared to independent (non-interacting) particles, then the number variance over balls centred at almost every point decays with exponent min(1,a) times a log term if a=1, over a possibly reduced range of scales for non-periodic systems. We apply this principle to eigenvalues of random N*N Girko matrices, leveraging results of Cipolloni et al., and obtain the optimal perimeter-like number variance, on the microscopic and some mesoscopic scales range, after local averaging. We also apply the results to Coulomb gases, by transferring the results of Serfaty: we prove that 2D-Coulomb gases are 2-hyperuniform, i.e. they have surface order number variance, which is optimal, and that 3D Coulomb gases are 1-hyperuniform. In 2D, it allows to prove finite Coulomb energy and Wasserstein distance to Lebesgue measure.
item.dc:creator: Rapha\"el Lachi\`eze-Rey (MATHNET, MAP5 - UMR 8145)

item.title: Efron type identities for stopping sets and Poisson hulls
item.description: arXiv:2608.06038v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a Poisson process $\eta$ on a general Borel space with intensity measure $\lambda$ and a stopping set $Z$ depending on $\eta$. Generalizing earlier results we prove a spatial Markov property for $Z$. In fact we establish this property for the larger class of finitely insertion tolerant random sets, which include pointwise limits of stopping sets. Using the spatial Markov property of $\eta$, we derive several distributional identities for the restrictions of $\eta$ and $\lambda$ to $Z$ and the complement of $Z$. An important special case in Euclidean space is the convex hull of a finite Poisson process. In this case our results generalize classical (and also more recent) identities connecting the number of vertices and the volume of the convex hull.
item.dc:creator: G\"unter Last, Ilya Molchanov

item.title: Spectral duality structures and the Fisher--Rao geometry of reset distributions
item.description: arXiv:2608.15805v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the geometry that spectral duality induces on the simplex of reset distributions for absorbed Markov processes with geometric resetting. In the Fisher--Rao metric, selected by \v{C}encov's theorem, the separatrix $\Sigma$ of reset-neutral distributions is rigid: under the square-root embedding $\pi\mapsto2\sqrt\pi$ its interior is a totally geodesic subsphere of the positive octant, itself a lower-dimensional Fisher--Rao simplex. The reset response reduces to a finite structure: the response functionals span a subspace whose dimension $r$ equals the number of active orbits of the duality involution, and the local separatrix is its annihilator. At the vertices of the simplex we prove a sign theorem valid for every $r$, which recovers the two-zone phenomenon of the first paper of this series. The invariant $r$ also settles the question of global orientation: for $r=1$, under a scalar sign condition satisfied by the canonical realisation, the sign of the response is fixed by the side of $\Sigma$; for $r\ge2$ the orientation cannot stay constant, and we give the criterion under which no global sign law holds, with counterexamples due to T. Newton showing that it is met in the abstract class. The biased random walk with multi-site geometric resetting realises the whole picture explicitly.
item.dc:creator: Juan Antonio Vega Coso

item.title: Hypocoercivity of Tempered Bouncy Particle Samplers for Heavy-Tailed Targets
item.description: arXiv:2608.29657v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the Tempered Bouncy Particle Sampler, a state-dependently tempered generalisation of the Bouncy Particle Sampler. Adapting the hypocoercivity framework of Dolbeault, Mouhot and Schmeiser (2010), we establish explicit, non-asymptotic exponential convergence bounds for a broad class of heavy-tailed targets that need not be log-concave or radially symmetric, including distributions with polynomial tails. The convergence rate is linked to the spectral gap of a tempered Langevin diffusion with the same invariant distribution, making a weighted Poincar\'e inequality the key assumption. We give admissible tempering choices for polynomial and stretched-exponential tails and derive mixing-time bounds with polynomial dependence on the dimension.
item.dc:creator: Aleksandar Mijatovi\'c, Vinayak Niraj

item.title: Angles and volumes of simplices, boxes, and crosspolytopes in constant curvature
item.description: arXiv:2609.21571v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine, up to isometry, the Riemannian tangent and normal cones at arbitrary faces of boxes, acute orthocentric simplices, rectangular simplices, and asymmetric crosspolytopes in spaces of constant sectional curvature $\kappa\in\mathbb R$. Using these descriptions, we derive explicit one-dimensional integral formulas for their internal and external angles in arbitrary dimension. In particular, our results cover regular simplices, cubes, and crosspolytopes, the three families of regular polytopes existing in every dimension. We also establish a correspondence between regular simplices and cubes with isometric local cones at corresponding faces, provided their edge-length parameters are suitably matched. Combining our angle formulas with the Poincar\'e relation, we obtain volume formulas for simplices and crosspolytopes in even dimensions. For boxes, we derive volume formulas valid in every dimension. Among the new results are angle formulas for spherical and hyperbolic cubes and crosspolytopes, volume formulas for asymmetric crosspolytopes, and a one-dimensional integral representation for the internal angles of regular crosspolytopes that appears to be new even in the Euclidean case. The formulas involve the standard normal distribution function $\Phi(x)$ and its values at purely imaginary arguments $\Phi(\mathrm{i} x)$. For example, if $d\geq 2$ is even, then the volume of the ideal regular simplex in the $d$-dimensional hyperbolic space of curvature $\kappa=-1$ is given by the absolutely convergent integral $$ \frac{\pi^{d/2}} {\sqrt{2}\,\mathrm{i}^{d}\, \Gamma\left(\frac{d+1}{2}\right)} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \left[ \Phi\left(\frac{\mathrm{i} y}{\sqrt d}\right)^{d+1} + \Phi\left(-\frac{\mathrm{i} y}{\sqrt d}\right)^{d+1} \right] \mathrm{e}^{-y^2/2}\,\mathrm{d}y. $$
item.dc:creator: Zakhar Kabluchko, Philipp Schange

item.title: Conditional Fluctuations of Mean-Field Systems with Stable Common Noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.01391v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study conditional fluctuations of smooth mean-field systems on a torus with endogenous symmetric stable common jumps of index $0<\alpha<1$. A positive-strip estimate makes empirical Poisson acceptance errors negligible at the sampling scale. The conditional laws given the full Poisson master converge in probability to a centered Gaussian kernel in a negative Sobolev path space. In dimension one, quantile coupling preserves this limit for microscopic marks with relative tail remainder $O(x^{-\rho})$, $\rho>\alpha/2$. A quantified second-order tail expansion gives the endogenous rank response: it shifts the conditional Gaussian mean at criticality and, when nonzero, dominates sampling below criticality. We also identify a separate stable-to-Brownian transition for the rank error. Finally, in a translation model, rank and clock couplings give the same microscopic laws. The rank coupling has a functional Gaussian limit. The clock coupling has no diverging additive path normalization at the limiting center.
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Autran

item.title: Second-order Wasserstein response for L\'evy laws
item.description: arXiv:2610.01411v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Weak perturbations of the same size can lead to terminal Wasserstein errors of different orders. For infinitely divisible laws smoothed by a Gaussian, we differentiate their distribution functions with respect to variance-weighted L\'evy characteristics. This includes distributional directions caused by moving atoms. We obtain first- and second-order expansions that are uniform over Lipschitz test functions. When the first response is nonzero, Gaussian analyticity gives the signed second coefficient of the Wasserstein--1 distance. When the first response vanishes, a finite second displacement moment is enough to obtain a quadratic response. Its coefficient is strictly positive if the displacement dispersion is nonzero. For local balanced remeshing, the error is comparable to the grid-alignment variance. This gives sharp quadratic grid rates for compactly supported densities and nonaligned atomic sequences. We derive metric speed and length along admissible non-atomic curves, and use the response to build a linear program with a proved bound on how much its error exceeds the infimum over the allowed class and consistent quadrature. We also prove a sharp transition as smoothing vanishes and give a multivariate second-order expansion. The appendix gives state-dependent response formulas and further stability estimates.
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Autran

item.title: Complexity of flows with interactions and stochastic analysis
item.description: arXiv:2610.06924v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study stochastic flows with interaction through an infinite-dimensional semigroup approach. By means of a kernel lifting procedure, we represent the solution to measure-valued stochastic equation as a Hilbert-valued Markov process. We identify its generator, construct the associated Markov semigroup, and establish a dense range condition using measure polynomial functionals. The results provide a framework for the analysis of stability of stochastic equations with interaction.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Shi

item.title: Metastability and Sharp Propagation-of-Chaos Thresholds for Mean-Field Interacting Diffusions on the Circle
item.description: arXiv:2610.08755v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study metastability and long-time propagation-of-chaos for mean-field interacting diffusions on the circle with multiple local free-energy minima. Working modulo rotations, we identify sharp exponential time scales for metastability and the validity and breakdown of the McKean-Vlasov approximation. Assuming finitely many critical rotation orbits and distinct local-minimum energies, we show that, for initial data in the attraction basin of a nonglobal minimum, metastability and propagation-of-chaos hold uniformly over deterministic times up to $e^{N(D-\varepsilon)}$ and fail at every deterministic sequence growing faster than $e^{N(D+\varepsilon)}$. Here $N$ is the particle number and $D$ the depth of the maximal Freidlin-Wentzell energy cycle having that minimum as its bottom. The same threshold governs running averages of the squared approximation error in a stronger pathwise sense, with corresponding metastability and propagation-of-chaos bounds for suitably aligned time-averaged empirical measures. When the global-minimum orbit is unique, we establish uniform-in-time propagation-of-chaos in its attraction basin without assuming finitely many critical orbits. The proofs develop the Freidlin-Wentzell cycle analysis for the empirical measure process and exploit Dawson and G\"artner's fixed-horizon large deviation estimates to analyze long excursions between metastable wells. We give a checkable Fourier criterion for finiteness of the critical orbits. We also investigate connections with phase transitions in the free-energy landscape, and discuss applications to the noisy Kuramoto and noisy transformer models. We provide, to our knowledge, the first sharp exponential-time analysis of the Dawson-G\"artner `tunnelling phenomenon' for general smooth interactions, with two-sided probability bounds and matching propagation-of-chaos thresholds.
item.dc:creator: Sayan Banerjee

item.title: Sandpile avalanches in two dimensions are finite
item.description: arXiv:2610.13940v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the abelian sandpile model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, a site with at least $2d$ grains topples by sending one grain to each neighbor. In a box $[-N,N]^d$ whose boundary absorbs grains, adding grains at random sites and toppling defines a Markov chain. Athreya and J\'arai (2004) constructed the stationary state on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ as the limit of its stationary distributions as $N\to\infty$. They asked whether, when a grain is added at the origin of a sandpile in the stationary state, the resulting avalanche of topplings is finite. J\'arai and Redig (2008) proved that the answer is yes for $d\geq 3$, using the transience of random walk. We prove, using a different method, that avalanches are also finite for $d=2$.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Bou-Rabee

item.title: Critical oriented percolation enhanced along random supercritical horizontal lines
item.description: arXiv:2610.18312v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the oriented site percolation model in a random environment introduced by Kesten, Sidoravicius and Vares (2022), in which the horizontal lines of the lattice are independently declared bad or good, sites being open with a probability that depends only on the type of their line. We study the boundary case where the bad lines are critical and the good ones supercritical, so that the model is critical oriented site percolation enhanced along a random set of good lines. We prove that percolation occurs for any positive density of the good lines. An arbitrarily sparse set of arbitrarily weakly enhanced lines suffices, the density of good lines and the strength of the enhancement being decoupled. The proof adapts the renormalization scheme of Archer, Hartarsky, Kolesnik, Olesker-Taylor, Schapira and Valesin (2026). We show that the edge of the process travels at a positive speed, which yields crossing estimates for tilted boxes; during runs of bad lines, we rely on the box-crossing property of Duminil-Copin, Tassion and Teixeira (2018); and the renormalized model dominates the oriented percolation with geometric defects of Hil\'ario, S\'a, Sanchis and Teixeira (2026).
item.dc:creator: Lucas Leproult, Maria Eul\'alia Vares

item.title: Strong Invariance Principle for Random Dirichlet Series
item.description: arXiv:2610.18353v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is shown that the random prime Dirichlet series $ X(s)=\sum_{p\in \mathcal{P}}\frac{\xi_p}{p^{s+1/2}} $ can be almost surely approximated by a Brownian motion, where $ \{\xi_p\}_{p\ge 1} $ are independent and identically distributed random variables with zero mean and finite variance, and $ \mathcal{P} $ is the set of prime numbers. As a consequence, the functional law of the iterated logarithm, limit laws of the iterated logarithm, and Chung's law of the iterated logarithm for $ X(s) $ are obtained. It is also shown that the random Dirichlet series $ Y(s)=\sum_{k=2}^{\infty} \frac{(\log k)^{\alpha}}{k^{s+1/2}} $ with $ \alpha=-1/2 $ admits the same approximation as $ X(s) $, and a direct relationship between $ X(s) $ and $ Y(s) $ with $ \alpha=-1/2 $ is established. The strong invariance principle for $ Y(s) $ with $ \alpha>-1/2 $ is also obtained.
item.dc:creator: Li-Xin Zhang

item.title: Monitoring for a Phase Transition in a Time Series of Wigner Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2507.04983v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop methodology and theory for the detection of a phase transition in a time-series of high-dimensional random matrices. In the model we study, at each time point \( t = 1,2,\ldots \), we observe a deformed Wigner matrix \( \mathbf{M}_t \), where the unobservable deformation represents a latent signal. This signal is detectable only in the supercritical regime, and our objective is to detect the transition to this regime in real time, as new matrix--valued observations arrive. Our approach is based on a partial sum process of extremal eigenvalues of $\mathbf{M}_t$, and its theoretical analysis combines state-of-the-art tools from random-matrix-theory and Gaussian approximations. The resulting detector is self-normalized, which ensures appropriate scaling for convergence and a pivotal limit, without any additional parameter estimation. Simulations show excellent performance for varying dimensions. Applications to pollution monitoring and social interactions in primates illustrate the usefulness of our approach.
item.dc:creator: Nina D\"ornemann, Piotr Kokoszka, Tim Kutta, Sunmin Lee

item.title: Sig-DEG for Distillation: Making Diffusion Models Faster and Lighter
item.description: arXiv:2508.16939v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Diffusion models achieve state-of-the-art generative performance but remain computationally expensive at inference, often requiring many discretization steps. We propose Sig-DEG (Signature-based Differential Equation Generator), a generator for distilling pre-trained diffusion models. Inspired by high-order stochastic Taylor expansions, Sig-DEG combines partial signatures that summarize Brownian motion over subintervals with a recurrent structure to approximate stochastic differential equation solutions to achieve universality. We formulate distillation as supervised learning, matching fine-resolution teacher trajectories on a coarse time grid. At inference, Sig-DEG enables fast generation, as the partial signatures can be simulated exactly from their known distributions without requiring fine-grained Brownian paths. Experiments on image and time-series generation demonstrate competitive sample quality with inference speedups of up to several hundred times over the teacher. A Schr\"odinger bridge example further demonstrates Sig-DEG's applicability beyond diffusion distillation.
item.dc:creator: Wen Ge, Lei Jiang, Lingyi Yang, Leonardo Roveri, Mingxuan Yi, Po-Yu Chen, Niels Cariou-Kotlarek, Francois Buet-Golfouse, Gaurav Mittal, Hao Ni

item.title: Rare Event Simulation of Quantum Error-Correcting Circuits
item.description: arXiv:2509.13678v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We describe a practical approach for accessing the logical failure rates of quantum error-correcting (QEC) circuits under low physical (component) failure rate regimes. Standard Monte Carlo is often the de facto approach for studying the failure rates of quantum circuits. However, in the study of fault-tolerant error-correcting circuits, the ability to extend this approach to low physical failure rates is limited. In particular, the use of Monte Carlo to access circuits that are relatively large or have high correcting power becomes more difficult as we lower the input failure rates of the individual components (gates) in the circuit. For these reasons, many simulations studying the circuit model go no lower than end-to-end logical failure rates in the 10^{-6} regime. In this report, we outline an approach that borrows from earlier work by Bravyi and Vargo to the more complex circuit noise model. Earlier works studied both the capacity and phenomenological noise models, but the work is insufficient for generating similar simulations in the circuit-noise model. To the best of our knowledge, our team is the first to develop a full prescription of the rare event simulation by splitting technique for the circuit-based noise model. We have also generated promising results that are confirmed by standard Monte Carlo simulation under an accessible regime. This work shows that we can access noise in the circuit-model prescription of quantum error-correcting code to failure rates below 10^{-20} regime.
item.dc:creator: Carolyn Mayer, Anand Ganti, Uzoma Onunkwo, Tzvetan Metodi, Benjamin Anker, Jacek Skryzalin

item.title: Approximate Bayesian computation for stochastic hybrid systems with empirically observed ergodic behaviour
item.description: arXiv:2511.11782v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Piecewise diffusion Markov processes (PDifMPs) form a versatile class of stochastic hybrid systems that combine continuous diffusion processes with discrete event-driven dynamics, enabling flexible modelling of complex real-world hybrid phenomena. The practical utility of PDifMP models, however, depends critically on accurate estimation of their underlying parameters. In this work, we present a novel framework for parameter inference in PDifMPs based on approximate Bayesian computation (ABC). Our contributions are threefold. First, we provide detailed simulation algorithms for PDifMP sample paths. Second, we extend existing ABC summary statistics for diffusion processes to account for the hybrid nature of PDifMPs, showing particular effectiveness for ergodic systems. Third, we demonstrate our approach on several representative example PDifMPs that empirically exhibit ergodic behaviour. Our results show that the proposed ABC method reliably recovers model parameters across all examples, even in challenging scenarios where only partial information on jumps and diffusion is available or when parameters appear in state-dependent jump rate functions. These findings highlight the potential of ABC as a practical tool for inference in various complex stochastic hybrid systems.
item.dc:creator: Sascha Desmettre, Agnes Mallinger, Amira Meddah, Irene Tubikanec

item.title: Minimax Binary Counting under Shuffle Privacy: Poisson Limits and Randomized-Response Optimality
item.description: arXiv:2603.10073v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study estimation of a deterministic binary count from the shuffled outputs of a common single-message local channel. Privacy is required for every neighboring composition at fixed global parameters $(\varepsilon,\delta)$, and estimators may be biased. We obtain uniform critical Poisson and Skellam approximations and characterize the limiting minimax risk as an infimum over finite observed-mark Poisson experiments. Let $\Lambda$ be the noise intensity required by the boundary Poisson-shift profile and let $\lambda_{\min}$ be the intensity required by the full composition-maximized randomized-response profile. Binary randomized response is asymptotically minimax optimal if and only if $\Lambda=\lambda_{\min}$. When $\Lambda<\lambda_{\min}$, the minimax value lies strictly between $(\Lambda+\lambda_{\min})/2$ and $\lambda_{\min}$, and a randomized-response construction with observed rare marks strictly improves on binary randomized response. We give a finite-sample certified example. Binary randomized response is strictly suboptimal at $\varepsilon=0$ for every $0<\delta<1$, and this persists for sufficiently small positive $\varepsilon$ at each fixed target. For every fixed positive $\varepsilon$, strict suboptimality also occurs along a sequence of fixed privacy targets tending to zero. The variational characterization permits approximation by finite marked channels; it does not assert that a finite optimizer exists.
item.dc:creator: Alex Shvets

item.title: Stochastic partial differential equation model for environmental DNA dynamics in river environments
item.description: arXiv:2608.03364v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) has emerged as a novel tool for quantifying the seasonal abundance of aquatic species in water bodies; however, its mathematical modeling is still at a germinating stage because of its mechanistic uncertainties. We propose a first-step mathematical and computational framework for the eDNA dynamics of migratory fish based on a novel stochastic partial differential equation model with a delayed source input. The model governs spatiotemporal eDNA concentration in rivers where the source comes from a stochastic differential equation for the migration dynamics of the fish. The affine nature of the model facilitates its theoretical analysis, including the guarantee of well-posedness and the closed-form derivation of the Laplace functional despite the proportionality coefficient of the multiplicative noise term being non-Lipschitz. We also propose a discretization scheme for the model that theoretically generates nonnegative numerical solutions. We finally apply the proposed model to eDNA concentration data sampled from midstream reaches of a river system and perform sensitivity analysis.
item.dc:creator: Hidekazu Yoshioka

item.title: Universality of the conformal anomaly
item.description: arXiv:2608.23201v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The sewing operation is the fundamental algebraic structure of the (infinite-dimensional) Segal moduli spaces as the conformal cobordism category. We prove a universal property of local $\mathbb{R}_+$-extensions of the sewing operation, characterizing them by one real parameter: their central charge. Our result is an analogue of ``Mumford's theorem,'' that appeared in Segal's monograph [Seg88, Seg04], classifying complex extensions, also known as one-dimensional modular functors. Algebraically, the real extensions are characterized by real-valued cocycles on pairs of surfaces under sewing. We identify the disk-disk cocycle as the universal Liouville action, also known as loop Loewner energy. The real determinant line bundle encodes the trace anomaly of euclidean two-dimensional conformal field theories (CFT) and the restriction function of Schramm-Loewner evolution (SLE) loop measures. It serves as the guiding example in our setup and proof strategy, providing the universal $\mathbb{R}_+$-extension. Our results thus give a mathematical explanation for the appearance of the central charge in CFT and SLE, and prove the conjectured uniqueness of Brownian loop measures as the canonical restriction function for SLE.
item.dc:creator: Sid Maibach, Eveliina Peltola

item.title: Polynomial mixing for stochastic viscous conservation law equation on the whole line
item.description: arXiv:2608.29824v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the long-time behavior of the viscous conservation law equation on the whole real line, subject to a white-in-time force and arbitrarily small damping and viscosity constants. We establish polynomial mixing rates in two settings: (a) a general super-quadratic flux with hyperviscous dissipation, where the growth of the nonlinearity is controlled by the order of hyperviscosity, and the force is sufficiently non-degenerate on a generic L2-basis; and (b) a general quadratic flux with standard second-order dissipation, and the force is non-degenerate on some unconditional basis. Both settings include the classical Burgers-type nonlinearity. The proof is based on an abstract polynomial coupling criterion developed in arXiv:2408.00592 and a Foia\c{s}--Prodi estimate.
item.dc:creator: Peng Gao, Liying Li

item.title: Algebra of spectral duality structures
item.description: arXiv:2609.04430v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper establishes the algebraic and categorical foundations of spectral duality structures (SDS). We show that the class of all SDS admits the structure of a graded symmetric monoidal category, where the degree $K$ is the fundamental invariant indexing the strata. We define operations of Cartesian product and disjoint union, morphisms preserving involution and weights, and prove that $C^\ast=1/(1+\sqrt K)$ is a functor constant on each stratum. We classify objects up to isomorphism by the combinatorial type $(k,f)$, the degree $K$, and a multiset of inversion classes $[r]=\{r,r^{-1}\}$. In each degree, skeletons are exactly the finite $C_2$-sets over the additive group of the reals with $C_2$ acting by $t\mapsto -t$, which explains the monoidal structure and identifies the classification with the decomposition into orbits. Furthermore, we prove that the response rank is the rank of an explicit matrix built from the amplitudes and the weights, and hence exactly the number of non-trivial pairs $k$ under the full-rank condition, and we connect the categorical structure with the Fisher--Rao geometry of Paper V. The SDS, originally discovered in stochastic resetting problems, is thus an autonomous mathematical object with a rich algebraic structure and a natural geometric realisation.
item.dc:creator: Juan Antonio Vega Coso

item.title: Asymptotics and finite sample bounds for prediction and smoothing in Wright-Fisher hidden Markov models
item.description: arXiv:2609.22444v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study signal prediction and smoothing in hidden Markov models whose latent signal is a multi-type Wright-Fisher diffusion and whose discrete-time observations are categorical. We consider a repeated-sampling regime with finitely many inspection times and large within-time samples.
